source.citation: John Moses, Illinois, Historical and Statistical: Comprising the Essential Facts of its Planting and Growth as a Province, County, Territory, and State. 2 vols. Chicago: Fergus Printing Co., 1889. A state history — the constitutions, the legislatures, the revenue, the internal-improvement scheme, the wars and the county formations — with biographical notice of the men who held state office.
what_it_does_not_supply: any Chicago address, household, trade or building
any evidence that a named family was in the town of Chicago in 1835 — the Newberry card names a surname the STATE history treats
any independent testimony: it is compiled from records and earlier histories, forty to fifty years after the fact
what_it_supplies: state-level context for 1835 Illinois: population, revenue, the count of counties, the internal-improvement scheme and the legislature that passed it
biographical notice of Illinois officeholders, which is what the Newberry index files its 418 cards on
a printed chronology against which a Chicago claim drawn from a county history can be cross-checked
